 During the rainy season, be vigilant about the risk of parasitic infections and worm infestations.
 VTV.vn - The humid environment during the rainy season increases the risk of exposure to parasites and worms, with roundworms from dogs and cats accounting for the majority of cases recorded in Dong Nai.
 Đài truyền hình Việt Nam • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Illustrative image.
 At the beginning of this year's rainy season, Mr. NVH (54 years old, residing in Phu Trung commune) came to Binh Phuoc General Hospital for examination due to prolonged skin itching, intermittent hives, and fatigue. Previously, he had undergone several allergy treatments, but his symptoms did not improve. Upon reviewing his medical history, the doctor noted that he kept many dogs at home and frequently interacted with them, but had not undergone regular deworming. Tests confirmed he was infected with canine roundworms (Toxocara). After treatment according to the prescribed protocol and lifestyle adjustments, his health gradually improved.
 This case demonstrates that parasitic diseases can manifest with symptoms easily confused with common illnesses, leading to prolonged treatment without the correct cause being identified.
 According to statistics from the Department of Parasitology and Entomology, Dong Nai Center for Disease Control (CDC), in 2025, the unit recorded 106 cases of intestinal worm infections, including 52 cases of roundworms, 3 cases of hookworms, and 51 cases of mixed infections. In addition, there were 165 cases of worm and fluke infections, including 158 cases of dog and cat roundworm infections, 5 cases of threadworm infections, and 2 cases of other parasitic infections.
 You may also like According to MSc. Vu Van Hiep, Deputy Head of the Department of Parasitology and Entomology, CDC Dong Nai, the rainy season creates favorable conditions for the eggs and larvae of many types of parasites to survive longer in the environment. Damp soil, potentially contaminated water sources, eating unwashed raw vegetables, walking barefoot, or contact with undewormed dogs and cats can all increase the risk of infection.
 Roundworm infections in dogs and cats can affect people of all ages, especially those who frequently come into contact with pets or environments contaminated with dog and cat feces. Many cases are asymptomatic and are only detected when symptoms persist.
 Dr. Mai Thi Ngoc Ha, from Phu Trung Commune Health Station, said that parasitic diseases often have nonspecific symptoms such as prolonged skin itching, recurrent hives, abdominal pain, digestive disorders, weight loss, anemia, or fatigue. In some cases, eosinophils may be found in blood tests. Depending on the type of parasite and the level of infection, the disease can cause damage to the liver, lungs, eyes, or other organs.
 People experiencing persistent itching of unknown origin, recurrent hives, persistent abdominal pain, or risk factors such as eating undercooked food, frequent contact with dogs or cats, or working in dirty environments should seek medical attention. Self-treating symptoms can prolong the illness and delay diagnosis.
 In 2025, the Dong Nai Health Department organized community deworming for 62,328 children aged 24 to under 60 months, achieving 99.4% of the plan; and deworming for 105,021 children aged 7 to 11 years, achieving 99.7% of the plan. Communication and monitoring activities for the prevention and control of parasitic diseases were also maintained in many localities.
 You may also like To prevent illness during the rainy season, people need to eat cooked food and drink boiled water; wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly; avoid eating raw meat, raw blood dishes, and undercooked food. They should use clean water, wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet, wear sandals when walking on damp ground, and prevent children from playing in sandy areas that may be contaminated.
 Families who own dogs and cats should deworm their pets regularly according to the veterinarian's instructions, collect and dispose of feces properly, and maintain hygiene in living areas and children's play areas. People should follow the deworming instructions of health officials , especially for children and high-risk groups; do not self-medicate if you suspect a parasitic infection.
